proseDefinitions.title: Base version and cumulative extension levels
proseDefinitions.details: Registered prefixes identify a developer. Successive levels for one BaseVersion are cumulative; BaseVersion can differ from document header/Catalog.Version. Existing ISO extension dictionaries are reused.

proseDefinitions.title: Enforce valid viewer preferences
proseDefinitions.details: Enforce permits only PrintScaling in this document, with a present valid preference other than AppDefault. Criteria for future names do not define additional names.

proseDefinitions.title: Collection folder graph and free identifiers
proseDefinitions.details: One root, globally unique non-negative ID, indirect Parent/Child/Next relationships, Parent absent on root; root-only Free ranges are inclusive low/high pairs and are updated on allocation.

proseDefinitions.title: Folder and file naming rules
proseDefinitions.details: PDF text names of 1–255 characters, no NUL, no /\:*"<>| and no final period. Siblings must be distinct after case normalization. EmbeddedFiles keys <ID>filename associate files with a folder; malformed keys belong to root.

proseDefinitions.title: Resource trees and relative IRIs
proseDefinitions.details: Navigator and collection resources have separate name trees mapping relative IRI text keys to simple streams. Parent-directory .. is forbidden. Rooted relative paths are container-root-relative. Navigator SWF supplies its own base; icon/header/welcome use container root.

proseDefinitions.title: Localized strings and API versions
proseDefinitions.details: Strings maps text IDs to localized text. Locale is UTS 35, hyphen and underscore equivalent. Versions follow m[.n[.p[.q]]] with absent components zero. Do not run a navigator requiring a newer APIVersion.

proseDefinitions.title: Explicit annotation and widget order
proseDefinitions.details: Tabs A follows Annots array order; Tabs W follows widgets in Annots array order, then remaining annotations by rows. Product-specific accessibility differences are implementation notes.

proseDefinitions.title: Projection annotations
proseDefinitions.details: Markup annotation subtype Projection composes common annotation and markup entries. A 3D measurement requires ExData subtype 3DM. Zero-height or zero-width Rect means AP is absent. It is meaningful only in an active associated runtime.

proseDefinitions.title: RichMediaExecute command targets
proseDefinitions.details: TA and TI are indirect references; TI must also be in target Instances. C names a script command; A can be a single text string/integer/real/boolean or an array of those typed arguments.

proseDefinitions.title: Signature locking and seed values
proseDefinitions.details: P=1/2/3 may only maintain or reduce prior MDP permissions. LockDocument has PDF name values true/false/auto, not booleans. Ff bits 8/9 constrain LockDocument/AppearanceFilter. Seed V=3 indicates extension-level-3 capability.

proseDefinitions.title: Barcode fields and appearances
proseDefinitions.details: Text field FT=Tx; barcode widgets require PMD. Single widget may merge with field; multiple widgets divide data among themselves. Numeric module values and ECC have symbology-dependent integer constraints; obsolete codeword fields are retained as source data.

proseDefinitions.title: Preserve XFA datasets
proseDefinitions.details: XFAResources is a name tree from text names to indirect streams containing xfa:datasets with xfa:data children, possibly XML signatures. The presence of this tree does not certify PDF/A conformance.

proseDefinitions.title: Register geographic coordinates
proseDefinitions.details: Viewport/Image/Form Measure subtype GEO maps unit-square LPTS pairs to GPTS latitude/longitude pairs in degrees. GCS required, DCS optional; coordinate dictionaries need EPSG or WKT. Bounds is optional unclosed neatline; PDU has three units in linear/area/angular order.

proseDefinitions.title: Geospatial point-cloud columns
proseDefinitions.details: PtData can be a dictionary or array of dictionaries in prose. Names defines tuple columns. Each XPTS member has the same arity; LAT/LON degrees and ALT meters are predefined numeric columns.

proseDefinitions.title: PRC support and node references
proseDefinitions.details: Stream subtype PRC extends level 1. View MS may only be M or absent for PRC. Node names derive from external PRC specification; PDF text encodings must be translated for comparison. Instance/Data applies only in rich-media context; RM also applies to ordinary 3D.

proseDefinitions.title: Persist measurement/comment associations
proseDefinitions.details: View.MA contains measurements visible only for that view. Measurement.S and Projection.ExData.M3DREF form explicit reciprocal indirect links when promoted to comments.

proseDefinitions.title: Linear-dimension markup geometry
proseDefinitions.details: Anchor points, annotation plane, text position and up direction define the linear markup. Text Y is the AP cross (A2-A1) direction oriented by TY; TP outside anchor interval creates an extension. V/U/UT and precision P produce a viewer-dependent label.

proseDefinitions.title: Perpendicular-dimension markup geometry
proseDefinitions.details: Leader lines parallel to D1 intersect a perpendicular measure line positioned by TP. Text follows A1 to A2, with up direction from plane cross X, oriented by TY; outlying text produces extension.

proseDefinitions.title: Angular-dimension markup geometry
proseDefinitions.details: Find direction-line center, radius ||TP-center||, leader intersections and angular arc. Parallel D1/D2 is invalid and produces no markup. TX must be orthogonal to AP; TY chooses up direction; DR determines degrees or radians.

proseDefinitions.title: Radial-dimension markup geometry
proseDefinitions.details: A1 center, A2 circle point, optional A3/A4 arc endpoints, TP arrow intersection and TX extension of EL define geometry. SC controls circle display and R radius versus diameter. Outlying arcs may need an extension arc.

proseDefinitions.title: 3D comment text box
proseDefinitions.details: A1 is geometry anchor; TP locates the closest box corner in current view. Text faces viewer. TB gives character columns and rows; font choice, flow and truncation are reader-dependent.

proseDefinitions.title: RichMedia activation and presentation
proseDefinitions.details: Inactive shows normal AP; active renders content according to annotation-specific Settings. Content can be shared. Scripts run in ordered per-annotation runtime. View/Configuration must be members of Content arrays. Floating window is non-printing, does not rotate or zoom, remains within reader presentation area; alignment depends on Lang.

proseDefinitions.title: RichMedia asset identity
proseDefinitions.details: Assets maps relative text filenames to filespec dictionaries whose F and UF both equal the key. Names are 1–255 characters, no NUL/:*"<>| or final period. Instance.Asset must refer to one of them and Subtype must match asset type. Configurations aggregate indirect instances.

proseDefinitions.title: Flash parameters, settings and compositing
proseDefinitions.details: Params is Flash-only. Foreground composites in order; Background uses last specified. Material needs BindingMaterialName. FlashVars and Settings are opaque text/stream data. Saving settings requires runtime edit rights and dirties document.

proseDefinitions.title: Cue points and actions
proseDefinitions.details: Flash cue points match by Name or Time to PDF cue-point actions; Time is milliseconds. Navigation chapters and generic Event semantics are distinct; sample A omission conflicts with table.

proseDefinitions.title: Save and restore view state
proseDefinitions.details: Snapshot can replace artwork image. View Params Instance points to active instance; opaque Data is captured with multimedia_getState or JavaScript StateEvent save and restored using multimedia_setState or StateEvent load. Video state example stores playhead seconds in stateData/movieInfo XML.

proseDefinitions.title: Bates-number artifact content
proseDefinitions.details: Pagination artifact subtype BatesN holds text Contents or array of texts for several Bates numbers. These can override start values in application-private Bates metadata; application controls order and formatting.

implementationNotes.scope: Adobe product implementation behavior; not a universal PDF requirement

In PDF 1.1, the number sign character (#) could be us ed as part of a name (for example, /A#B), and the 
specifications did not specifically prohibit embedded spaces (although Adobe producer applications 
did not provide a way to write names containing them). In PDF 1.2, the number sign became an escape 
character, preceding two hexadecimal digits. Thus, a 3-character name A-space-B can now be written 
as /A#20B (since 20 is the hexadecimal code for the space character). This means that the name /A#B is 
no longer valid, since the number sign is not followed by two hexadecimal digits. A name object with 
this value must be written as /A#23B, since 23 is the hexadecimal code for the character #.

implementationNotes.scope: Adobe product implementation behavior; not a universal PDF requirement
implementationNotes.textAsExtracted:
In cases where a PostScript name must be preserve d or where a string is permitted in PostScript but 
not in PDF, the Acrobat Distiller application uses the # convention as necessary. When an Acrobat 
viewer generates PostScript, it inverts the convention by writing a string where permitted or a name 
otherwise. For example, if the string (Adobe Green) were used as a key in a dictionary, Distiller would 
use the name /Adobe#20Green and the viewer would generate (Adobe Green).

implementationNotes.scope: Adobe product implementation behavior; not a universal PDF requirement

In Acrobat 4.0 and earlier versions, a name object being treated as text is typically interpreted in a host 
platform encoding, which depends on the operating system and the local language. For Asian 
languages, this encoding may be something like Shift-JIS or Big Five. Consequently, it is necessary to 
distinguish between names encoded this way and ones encoded as UTF-8. Fortunately, UTF-8 
encoding is very stylized and its use can usually be recognized. A name that does not conform to UTF-8 
encoding rules can instead be interpreted according to host platform encoding.

Interaction between accessibility preference and annotation tab order
This note clarifies the viewer-specific behavior of different Acrobat versions relative to annotation tab 
order and the accessibility preference selection.
Beginning in PDF 1.5, the user experience of tabbing between annotations on a page (tab order) can be 
made explicit by means of the page object Tabs entry (see Table 3.27). However, when this entry is not 
defined, Acrobat tab order varies depending on the Acrobat version and on accessibility preference 
settings. This behavior is viewer-specific because it is not specified by the PDF specification. Because the 
row, column, and structured tab order settings behave exactly as specified in the PDF specification, they 
do not have a viewer-specific behavior.
The Acrobat Preferences dialog box presents an Accessibility window. The Tab Order panel in that window 
has a check box titled “Use document structure for tab order when no explicit tab order is specified. ” 
Selecting that check box specifies accessibility preferences.
Regardless of the Acrobat accessibility preference setting, the following applies to (a) all Acrobat versions 
when processing a PDF document that omits a Tabs entry or (b) Acrobat 5 or earlier when processing a 
PDF document regardless of a Tabs entry:
● If the document is structured (contains tagging), the annotations are visited in structure order. 
● Otherwise, widgets are visited in the order in which they appear in the Annots array, and then other 
annotation types are visited in row order. 
Note: Documents that conform to PDF version 1.5 or earlier have no Tabs entries.
Accessibility preference selected (default setting)

when the accessibility preference is selected:
● If the document is viewed with Acrobat 6 or later and is structured, the Tabs entry affects tab order as 
follows: 
Widget order: When Tabs is set to W, widgets are visited in the order in which they appear in the 
Annots array and then other annotation types are visited in structure order. Acrobat 9 and later 
support Widget order. 
All other tab orders: Annotations are visited as specified in the PDF specification supported by the 
particular version of Acrobat. Acrobat 6 and later support increasingly specific levels of tab order.
● If the document omits a Tabs entry or when the document is viewed with Acrobat 5 or earlier, the 
presence of structure (tagging) affects tab order as follows:
Structured: Annotations are visited in structure order. 
Not structured: Widgets are visited in the order in which they appear in the Annots array, and 
then other annotation types are visited in row order. 
Note: Documents that conform to PDF version 1.5 or earlier have no Tabs entries.
Accessibility preference not selected
The following bulleted items explains Acrobat behavior relative to annotation tab order when the 
accessibility preference is not selected. 
The document is viewed with Acrobat 9.
Widget order: When Tabs is set to W, widgets are visited in the order in which they appear in the 
Annots array, and then other annotation types are visited in row order.
All other tab orders (row, column, structure, and annotation): Annotations are visited as 
specified by the PDF specification.
No Tabs entry: Widget annotations are ordered as they appear in the Annots array, followed by 
other annotation types ordered by rows. 
● The document is viewed with Acrobat 6, 7, or 8.
Tabs entry provided: Tab order is as specified by the Tabs entry. These versions support only the 
column, row, and structure order settings. 
No Tabs entry or the Tabs entry value not recognized: Widgets are visited in the order in which 
they appear in the Annots array, and then other annotation types are visited in row order. 
● For a document viewed with Acrobat 5 or earlier, widgets are visited in the order in which they appear

Acrobat provides various user-specified options fo r determining how the region specified by the crop 
box is to be imposed on the output medium during printing. Although these options have varied from 
one Acrobat version to another, the default behavior is as follows: 
1. Select the media size and orientation according to the operating system’s Print Setup dialog. 
(Acrobat has no direct control over this process.) 
2. Compute an effective crop box by clipping it with  the media box and rotating the page according to 
the page object’s Rotate entry, if specified. 
3. Center the crop box on the medium, rotating it if necessary to enable it to fit in both dimensions. 
4. Optionally, scale the page up or down so that th e crop box coincides with the edges of the medium 
in the more restrictive dimension. 
The description above applies only in simple printing workflows that lack any other information about 
how PDF pages are to be imposed on the output medium. In some workflows, there is additional 
information, either in the PDF file (BleedBox, TrimBox, or ArtBox) or in a separate job ticket (such as 
JDF or PJTF). In these circumstances, other rules apply, which depend on the details of the workflow. 
Consequently, it is recommended that PDF files initially be created with the crop box the same as the 
media box (or equivalently, with the crop box omitted). This ensures that if the page is printed on that 
size medium, the crop box coincides with the edges of the medium, producing predictable and 
dependable positioning of the page contents. On the other hand, if the page is printed on a different 
size medium, the page may be repositioned or scaled in implementation-defined or user-specified 
ways.

implementationNotes.section: Implementation Notes to Adobe Extensions to ISO 32000

Acrobat 9.0 Pro has two standard navigators and several custom navigators. When an Acrobat user 
chooses a custom navigator while in authoring mode, Acrobat embeds the navigator in the portable 
collection. After being embedded and saved, all editions of Acrobat and Adobe Reader, beginning with

The custom navigator that Acrobat Pro embeds into the portable collection is a stand-alone file 
available on the local hard drive. A navigator file collects into a single file, the resources required by a 
navigator of a portable collection. Although PDF 1.7 supports two standard collection views (tile and 
details), a navigator provides a custom view using a SWF file. The navigator SWF file interacts with a 
host authoring or viewing application through Acrobat ActionScript API. See the Acrobat ActionScript 
API Reference in the Bibliograph
y.

implementationNotes.textAsExtracted:
Older viewers—earlier than 9.0—ignore and do  not process the additional approval signature 
FieldMDP Lock state. To increase compatibility, Acrobat sets FieldMDP to lock all fields when the 
document is locked. Consequently, older viewers consider all fields locked when the document lock is

Documents signed with Acrobat 9.0 with locking, and then opened and modified in an older viewer 
(adding annotations), and then opened in Acrobat 9.0 show invalidated signatures.

implementationNotes.section: Implementation Notes to Adobe Extensions to ISO 32000
implementationNotes.scope: Adobe product implementation behavior; not a universal PDF requirement
implementationNotes.textAsExtracted:
How seed values are interpreted is both applicat ion-specific and specific to the signature handler 
associated with the signature field. Each application and handler may choose how to honor the seed 
values. The behavior of Acrobat and the PPKLite signature handler is documented below for the 
LockDocument seed value, and for AppearanceFilter in implementation note E-15.
A seed value of auto specifies that the implementation is application-specific. Acrobat processes the 
auto value as follows: If the document contains hidden fields, the signer is not allowed to lock the 
document. Otherwise, the signer can choose whether to lock at the time of signing, with the same 
behavior as the value being set to false and the required flag not set. Acrobat does not honor the 
required flag when the LockDocument value is auto.

implementationNotes.textAsExtracted:
The AppearanceFilter is implemented as follows: If the AppearanceFilter is present, it 
automatically chooses a matching appearance from the user interface. If the AppearanceFilter is 
optional, and if a matching appearance is not available, it defaults to the normal behavior where any 
appearance can be chosen. If the filter is required, the matching appearance is selected and the

implementationNotes.scope: Adobe product implementation behavior; not a universal PDF requirement
implementationNotes.textAsExtracted:
Acrobat Pro and Acrobat Pro Extended while in po rtable collection editing mode use the combination 
of ID, Locale, and Version to uniquely identify a navigator. This behavior allows the application to 
determine that the navigator embedded in a collection is the same as a navigator description stored on 
hard disk. IDs can be human-readable or a URN based on a machine-generated GUID, as long as they 
are likely to be unique. GUIDs are defined in RFC4122, A Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) URN 
Namespace, listed in the Bibliography.

implementationNotes.section: Implementation Notes to Adobe Extensions to ISO 32000
implementationNotes.scope: Adobe product implementation behavior; not a universal PDF requirement
implementationNotes.textAsExtracted:
For version 9.0, a PDF viewing application loads the navigator found in the PDF file, no matter what 
navigators are available.
In addition to loading the navigator in the PDF file, a portable collection authoring application—
Acrobat Pro or Acrobat Pro Extended—loads the navigator with the highest version number when it 
finds more than one with the same ID and locale. Acrobat, in authoring mode, usually shows the PDF 
file's navigator as well as all the loaded navigators. If one of the loaded navigators matches the PDF 
file's navigator (ID, version, locale), only one copy is shown in the navigator list. If the PDF file's 
navigator is newer (higher version number), only it is shown. If the PDF file's navigator is older, both are 
shown, with the loaded navigator marked as new.

sourceAnomalies.title: PtData type
sourceAnomalies.description: Tables 4.39, 4.45 and 8.109 declare PtData as a dictionary, while the prose on page 53 permits a dictionary or an array of point-data dictionaries. The model permits the explicitly documented union and preserves both source statements.

sourceAnomalies.title: 9.51a Name
sourceAnomalies.description: Table 9.51a prints the nonexistent PDF type “text tree” for Name. The Configuration01 example on page 95 uses a text string, which is the recorded interpretation; a text tree is not interpreted as a name tree.

sourceAnomalies.title: CuePoint.A
sourceAnomalies.description: Table 9.51e requires CuePoint.A, but the Navigation examples on pages 92 and 96 omit it. The model retains the table requirement and identifies the examples as incomplete rather than inventing an unstated conditional rule.

sourceAnomalies.title: ProjectionExData.Type
sourceAnomalies.description: Table 9.39g labels ProjectionExData.Type required and then says “if present”. The model follows the explicit required qualifier while preserving the contradictory wording.

sourceAnomalies.title: Algorithm3.12 Owner
sourceAnomalies.description: Algorithm 3.12 refers to the user password in its body, although its title and O/owner-salt/U formula authenticate the owner. The formula is preserved and the role is interpreted as owner.

sourceAnomalies.title: Algorithm3.2a control flow
sourceAnomalies.description: Algorithm 3.2a numbers owner and user branches consecutively without an explicit return. Successful owner authentication recovers OE and returns that key; it does not fall through into the user branch. Neither matching password is an authentication failure.

sourceAnomalies.title: AES padding
sourceAnomalies.description: Algorithm 3.1a omits an explicit padding instruction, while AESV3 in table 3.22 specifies CBC padding. In contrast, algorithms 3.8/3.9 explicitly wrap UE/OE without padding, and Perms uses one unpadded ECB block. Those three modes remain distinct.

sourceAnomalies.title: Perms EncryptMetadata
sourceAnomalies.description: The Algorithm 3.2a summary mentions Perms magic and P but omits byte 8. Algorithm 3.13 additionally requires the T/F byte to agree with EncryptMetadata; validation includes that check.

sourceAnomalies.title: Length unités
sourceAnomalies.description: Table 3.22 expresses Length in bits and visually extends the former 40–128 range to 256. Encryption-dictionary Length and crypt-filter Length must be distinguished: the interoperable R=5 writer uses a 256-bit encryption entry and the established 32-byte AESV3 crypt-filter entry, retaining the source wording separately.

sourceAnomalies.title: SASLprep truncation
sourceAnomalies.description: The 127-byte limit applies after SASLprep and UTF-8 encoding. Truncation may split a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence; it is byte truncation rather than a 127-character limit.

sourceAnomalies.title: XFA extensionlevels
sourceAnomalies.description: Page 42 associates XFA 2.5/2.6 with extension levels 1/2; note E5 attributes both to Acrobat 8.1; note 1 lists XFA 2.6/2.7/2.8 for extension levels 1/2/3. These inconsistent mappings are retained separately.

sourceAnomalies.title: 3Dunits scaling
sourceAnomalies.description: The prose on pages 59–60 states that m model units equal n physical units, implying n/m, whereas page 61 prints Y=(m/n)*X. Callers explicitly choose UnitDescription or PrintedEquation; neither is silently selected as the universal interpretation.

sourceAnomalies.title: Angular U
sourceAnomalies.description: Page 70 refers to an angular label string U, but table 9.39d contains no U entry and uses DR for degrees/radians. No U entry is invented without another source.

sourceAnomalies.title: PaperMetaData XSymHeight
sourceAnomalies.description: XSymHeight is marked required but described as needed only for PDF417. Its conditional scope is retained instead of imposing it on every barcode symbology.

sourceAnomalies.title: PaperMetaData nCodeWordRow/Col
sourceAnomalies.description: nCodeWordRow and nCodeWordCol have no required qualifier, are marked obsolete and default to zero. They are not made mandatory.

sourceAnomalies.title: BarcodeBG
sourceAnomalies.description: Note E7 calls MK.BG=[1.0] black, whereas DeviceGray 1 denotes white. This product-note error does not define a new color conversion rule.

sourceAnomalies.title: RichMediaParams.Settings
sourceAnomalies.description: RichMediaParams.Settings has no explicit required qualifier and defaults to undefined. It remains optional with opaque runtime settings.

sourceAnomalies.title: RichMediaWindow.Height
sourceAnomalies.description: RichMediaWindow.Height repeats the width wording. Height is a distinct numeric child dictionary, with its printed Default/Max/Min values 216/432/72.

sourceAnomalies.title: RichMediaWindow.Position reference
sourceAnomalies.description: Several cross-references are misnumbered: RichMediaWindow.Position points to 9.50e rather than 9.50f; Presentation names “Table 5”; Animation and Binding cite wrong pages; some 8.111d and 9.39 references are malformed. The actual table locators are recorded.

sourceAnomalies.title: RichMedia example booleans
sourceAnomalies.description: The RichMedia example uses /false for Toolbar, NavigationPane and PassContextClick, which are name objects rather than booleans. Constructed values use the boolean false.

sourceAnomalies.title: RichMedia instance array
sourceAnomalies.description: The instance arrays on pages 89 and 95 use “0 obj” where indirect references require “0 R”. The invalid example syntax is not reproduced as an executable fixture.

sourceAnomalies.title: RichMedia examples object links
sourceAnomalies.description: The extended RichMedia example is incomplete: Settings refers to object 22 although that object is a View and Settings is 23; Content.Views points to Instances; a view has an unnamed dictionary instead of Params; Presentation object 24 and some assets/streams are absent. It is not treated as a valid complete fixture.

sourceAnomalies.title: RichMedia activation example
sourceAnomalies.description: The activation example uses WhenClicked, but table 9.50a defines XA, PO and PV. XA is the specified explicit activation value.

sourceAnomalies.title: CuePoint subtype example
sourceAnomalies.description: The cue-point example uses Nav, while table 9.51e defines Navigation and Event. The model uses Navigation.

sourceAnomalies.title: RichMedia Assets naming example
sourceAnomalies.description: The Assets example maps Player.swf to object 31, whose F/UF entries name Flash.swf. A corrected independent example must make the asset-tree key agree with the file specification.

sourceAnomalies.title: Navigator String vs Strings
sourceAnomalies.description: Navigator prose uses singular String, while table 8.6d names the entry Strings. The model uses Strings.

sourceAnomalies.title: AnnotationTabs note77
sourceAnomalies.description: Note 77 claims PDF 1.5 or earlier has no Tabs entry, while table 3.27 introduces Tabs in PDF 1.5. The contradictory product note is not used as a version gate.

sourceAnomalies.title: Notes gaps/duplications
sourceAnomalies.description: Implementation note 6 is absent; note 10 repeats a paragraph; table 9.39 repeats MA; an AppearanceFilter cross-reference names E15 instead of E16. These source gaps and duplicates remain identifiable in the inventory.

sourceAnomalies.title: Algorithm 3.2 password padding omission
sourceAnomalies.description: The supplement rewrites Algorithm 3.2 step 1 as PDFDocEncoding conversion but omits the inherited mandatory 32-byte password padding/truncation. ISO 32000-1 Algorithm 2, PDF pages 69–70, specifies the padding bytes and length. The implementation preserves that inherited rule, verified against independent qpdf R=2/R=3/R=4 keys.

implementedChanges.title: Explicit freeing, generation advancement and reuse across complete revision indexes

clauses.title: Compatibility with Applications That Do Not Support Compressed Reference Streams

implementedBehavior: Immutable release/reuse operations distinguish unused generation-zero holes from deleted generations and retain exact retired record/byte-span history.
Linked type-0 lists preserve the object-zero generation-65535 head, tail zero, deletion increment, stored reuse generation and permanent generation-65535 entries.

semanticConstraints: No identifier receives conflicting operations in one revision; generation saturation never wraps or becomes live.
ObjStm containers and members remain generation zero and never take a reused/free number; remembered initial holes cannot bypass this rule later.
Hybrid generation-65535 compatibility shadows for live compressed members are not reusable free entries.
A container can be released only if all its still-live compressed members are released; optional obsolete references are allowed as null but required effective Resources cannot disappear.

validation.independentResult: 90 histories / 450 PDFs under each PHP 8.3/8.4/8.5; all three xref layouts, ordinary/linearized initial files, nine plain/R2/R3/R4/R5 security cases, generation-zero holes and generation-one/two delete/reuse transitions. implementedChanges.title: Applied field seed/lock/backend/output verification and historical signing constraints

clauses.title: Signature lock and appearance consumer behavior

implementedBehavior: Explicit field/reservation/seed/lock/intent/backend composition negotiates actual Filter/SubFilter/Reason/digest/parser/certificate/appearance choices and copies FieldMDP transforms/Data scope.

Preflight and finalization read the actual frozen emitted field/seed/catalogue/appearance and verify the real cryptographic output against exact input/output hashes and the expected signing credential.

semanticConstraints: Perms/DocMDP is optional under Table254; a certification field alone detects changes and the optional catalogue link adds prevention.

Native DSA/SHA256 remains available when SV.DigestMethod is absent, including an empty or Reasons-only SV; DSA/SHA1 applies at the present DigestMethod entry. This Table234/Table257 interpretation is explicit, not an official erratum.

implementedChanges.title: Replaceable variable-text sections in supplied editable example appearances
